A working answer is credible enough for an explicitly qualified model, not verified server behavior. Confidence applies to the stated finding, not every effect of that class. An implementation gap is not a request for a game experiment.

## Prioritized follow-up

Each queue is ordered by priority, then stable ID. A question can have partial tests at several stages; these queue counts must not be added together as distinct questions. Accepted-answer corroboration and out-of-scenario work remain inside their records, not in these pending queues.

### Current beta · level 30

An experiment within the announced current level-30 beta cap, subject to actual realm access and listed prerequisites. Existing level-20 observations do not certify later ranks.

- **High · [CORE-001 — Boss attack tables](#core-001)**
  - Prerequisites: Known skill/hit, an equal-level and a +3-level target, recorded facing.
  - Observe / verify: Count white/special/ranged outcomes separately; compare queued and unqueued attacks. This supplies a low-level table, not a level-63 certification.
- **High · [CORE-002 — Energy regeneration and haste](#core-002)**
  - Prerequisites: Two known general-haste totals, identical resource talents, uncapped recovery windows and precise resource timestamps.
  - Observe / verify: Repeat matched recovery cycles from low Energy to below the cap, with no attacks or refunds. Aggregate endpoint uncertainty; a single rounded 1% window is insufficient. Run an attack-speed-only control separately.
- **High · [CORE-003 — Energy refunds on avoided attacks](#core-003)**
  - Prerequisites: A Rogue with builders/Eviscerate/Rupture, or a level-20 Cat with Claw/Rake/Rip; uncapped Energy and an avoidance-producing target.
  - Observe / verify: Pair resource changes and combo points with each avoided action; subtract independently measured regeneration. Test builders and finishers separately.
- **High · [CORE-004 — Spell GCD versus physical GCD](#core-004)**
  - Prerequisites: Known casting-speed modifier, one magical instant and one physical 1.5-second action; client cooldown timestamps.
  - Observe / verify: Compare GCD duration independently of cast time. Only test the floor when enough haste is actually available; a 1% modifier cannot establish it.
- **High · [CORE-005 — Channel speed sources](#core-005)**
  - Prerequisites: Arcane Missiles and separately isolated Berserking or Wind Blessed; all missile timestamps.
  - Observe / verify: Compare complete channel duration and tick spacing with a no-modifier control, excluding Missile Barrage.
- **High · [CORE-014 — Mana restoration threat](#core-014)**
  - Prerequisites: A mana user, effective mana potions, threat API readings and one versus several engaged enemies.
  - Observe / verify: Measure total and per-enemy threat from one isolated return, including same-type and mixed-type packs. A mana-capped use is the wasted-resource control.
- **High · [DATA-001 — Server downranking penalties](#data-001)**
  - Prerequisites: Two learned ranks of a caster damage spell, controlled SP-only gear changes, fixed target level/resistance and no changing damage talents.
  - Observe / verify: Compare the damage slope per SP at each rank, not their raw hit sizes. Record exact player level and exclude crits; repeat after leveling if possible.
- **High · [DRU-001 — Omen of Clarity proc frequency](#dru-001)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-20 Druid with trained Omen, no other Clearcasting sources and event timestamps.
  - Observe / verify: After each ten-second cooldown, count direct eligible events before the next proc. Compare autos, direct spells and heals; do not count periodic ticks as direct casts.
- **High · [DRU-003 — Form weapon damage and flat imbues](#dru-003)**
  - Prerequisites: Bear and level-20 Cat, matched-stat weapons with substantially different DPS, plus an obtainable flat-damage enchant/imbue.
  - Observe / verify: Compare form attack damage at fixed AP; test the flat effect independently from the weapon swap.
- **High · [DRU-005 — Bear threat multipliers](#dru-005)**
  - Prerequisites: Bear, white attacks/Swipe, precise threat readings, known damage and no Thorns/proc interference.
  - Observe / verify: First determine the form multiplier from ordinary hits, then Swipe's additional threat; include multiple enemies without duplicating totals.
- **High · [DRU-011 — Proc enchants in animal forms](#dru-011)**
  - Prerequisites: Only if an enchanted weapon can actually be supplied in the beta; an obtainable enchant is not established by a low character-level requirement.
  - Observe / verify: Compare isolated caster-form and Cat/Bear attacks with proc timestamps and equipped/form weapon speeds.
- **High · [DRU-012 — Bear outgoing and incoming rage formulas](#dru-012)**
  - Prerequisites: Bear, uncapped rage, no Maul/Enrage/Primal Fury and matched attack speed while damage varies.
  - Observe / verify: Separate ordinary hits, crits and avoided swings. For incoming rage stop autos and vary armor independently from maximum health.
- **High · [HUN-001 — Pet owner-stat inheritance](#hun-001)**
  - Prerequisites: Hunter or Warlock pet, one isolated owner-stat change and pet API/damage observations.
  - Observe / verify: Prioritize demon AP/SP/mana and pet update timing; keep owner and external pet buffs distinct. Do not repeat every accepted Hunter coefficient merely because a server script is hidden.
- **High · [HUN-002 — Pet per-hit damage versus speed](#hun-002)**
  - Prerequisites: Two same-family/same-level pets of different speeds and two owner AP totals.
  - Observe / verify: Compare the change in pet damage per hit across the AP delta for each speed; control happiness and training. This separates an AP coefficient from the already observed base-speed difference.
- **High · [PAL-001 — Seal of Righteousness spell-power formula](#pal-001)**
  - Prerequisites: Same low-rank seal, target and recorded weapon speed; two known personal-SP values and one-/two-hand controls.
  - Observe / verify: Measure proc damage slopes without Judgement of the Crusader, then add that target bonus separately. Keep weapon damage, talents and crit outcomes controlled.
- **High · [PAL-005 — Seal of Fury and its judgement](#pal-005)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-10/18 Seal of Fury and a shield.
  - Observe / verify: Validate the implemented low-rank proc damage and absorb relationship; use PAL-006 for replacement/depletion behavior.
- **High · [PAL-006 — Seal of Fury shield replacement and mana](#pal-006)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-20 Paladin with the talent, shield, Seal of Fury, known attacker levels and uncapped mana.
  - Observe / verify: Observe successive procs before damage, partial/full depletion, expiry and replacement. Compare equal-level and up-to-three-level-higher attackers; record absorb and mana events separately.
- **High · [PAL-008 — Vindication's target AP reduction](#pal-008)**
  - Prerequisites: One-point Vindication at 20 and matched enemy swings.
  - Observe / verify: Optional validation of the target aura and damage reduction, without confusing owner AP growth with enemy AP loss.
- **High · [WAR-003 — Incoming rage and mitigation](#war-003)**
  - Prerequisites: Nonattacking Warrior, fixed enemy, independent armor and maximum-health changes; no concurrent rage abilities.
  - Observe / verify: Compare uncapped rage per pre-armor and post-armor damage across the reported threshold. Include shielded and unshielded hits without changing the other stats.
- **High · [WAR-008 — Shield attacks and weapon procs](#war-008)**
  - Prerequisites: Shield Bash, shield and an actually obtainable known weapon proc; autos stopped.
  - Observe / verify: Count proc events following isolated Bashes. This is a partial test, not certification of Shield Slam or Windfury.
- **High · [WL-009 — Demonic Knowledge ranked values](#wl-009)**
  - Prerequisites: Demonic Knowledge accessible with enough talent/legacy points; fixed owner and active pet.
  - Observe / verify: Measure owner/pet stats at each reachable rank and despawn/resummon; record unavailable ranks.
- **Medium · [CORE-009 — Eureka cast and periodic bonuses](#core-009)**
  - Prerequisites: Gnome Mage/Warlock/Priest with a low-rank DoT or channel; exact build and buff-stack timestamps.
  - Observe / verify: Repeat those three cases in game. Do not infer intended behavior from an open bug report or conflate the old mana-discount amount with current values.
- **Medium · [CORE-010 — Read Ley Line regeneration](#core-010)**
  - Prerequisites: High Order mana user; fixed Spirit, a known MP5 item delta, uncapped mana and no other temporary regen.
  - Observe / verify: Compare idle and continuous-spending recovery with the short buff. Record application/expiration and test the long location buff separately if needed.
- **Medium · [CORE-015 — Weapon-racial crit and ranged attacks](#core-015)**
  - Prerequisites: Human or Orc Hunter and matching versus nonmatching melee weapons with equal Agility/crit stats; unchanged ranged weapon and pet.
  - Observe / verify: Record melee, ranged, spell and pet crit APIs before/after the swap, then compare ranged attack outcomes if the display and source descriptions disagree. Check one and two matching weapons separately rather than assuming the bonus stacks.
- **Medium · [DRU-014 — Faerie Fire announced cost/cooldown versus captured data](#dru-014)**
  - Prerequisites: Caster Faerie Fire access and enough mana for cost observation.
  - Observe / verify: Record mana delta, cooldown availability and spell ID; isolate Spirit/MP5 ticks.
- **Medium · [HUN-003 — Pet external buffs and action cadence](#hun-003)**
  - Prerequisites: Only if pet cadence sensitivity proves material; a trained damage ability and a resource trace.
  - Observe / verify: Compare ability use when resource-limited versus resource-capped. Do not mix this with owner inheritance or ordinary spell cooldowns.
- **Medium · [HUN-007 — Pet families and new trained abilities](#hun-007)**
  - Prerequisites: A family actually tameable by level 20 and its first trained rank.
  - Observe / verify: Confirm learning, resource cost and damage/cooldown for that family. This does not establish higher-rank availability.
- **Medium · [HUN-012 — Savage Strikes article/client version conflict](#hun-012)**
  - Prerequisites: Savage Strikes access and matched talent-on/off attacks at fixed AP, weapon and target.
  - Observe / verify: Separate hit-size changes from crit-frequency changes, and record build/ability IDs.
- **Medium · [MAG-005 — Clearcasting and Missile Barrage event ordering](#mag-005)**
  - Prerequisites: Arcane Concentration, Arcane Missiles and mana/aura/tick logging without other proc talents.
  - Observe / verify: Cast isolated complete and cancelled channels; count Clearcasting procs and identify whether a pre-existing proc is spent at channel start or completion.
- **Medium · [PAL-004 — Holy melee partial resistance](#pal-004)**
  - Prerequisites: Holy Strike and seal attacks against targets of known equal and higher levels; fixed damage inputs.
  - Observe / verify: Inspect explicit resisted amounts and damage clusters separately from miss/dodge outcomes. A small sample with no resist is not proof of immunity.
- **Medium · [PAL-007 — Hammer of the Righteous availability](#pal-007)**
  - Prerequisites: Trainer/spellbook UI with unavailable future ranks visible, if the beta exposes them.
  - Observe / verify: Capture an actual offering and requirement. No fixed later test level can be promised until this evidence exists.
- **Medium · [PAL-010 — Retribution Aura provider scaling](#pal-010)**
  - Prerequisites: Paladin level 16 or Druid with Thorns, two controlled caster-SP values, distinct recipient and fixed enemy.
  - Observe / verify: Measure the coefficient and swap caster gear after application to distinguish intended dynamic behavior from the known beta snapshot bug. Do not change recipient SP simultaneously.
- **Medium · [PRI-002 — Death backlash and Dark Sacrifice modifiers](#pri-002)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-20 Undead Priest with Dark Sacrifice, fixed maximum health and Spirit, uncapped mana, with/without a controlled absorb.
  - Observe / verify: Record each health and mana delta, then repeat near mana cap and low health. Separate periodic dummy returns from ordinary Spirit regeneration.
- **Medium · [PRI-003 — Inner Focus periodic crit behavior](#pri-003)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-20 Priest with Inner Focus and a DoT in its crit mask.
  - Observe / verify: Compare three arms: no aura, aura activated after the DoT and held, and aura consumed by applying the DoT. Record enough ticks and the exact build; separate live observation from intended design.
- **Medium · [SCEN-005 — General absorb-pool and shielding threat](#scen-005)**
  - Prerequisites: Priest with Power Word: Shield, a cooperating player and a controlled hostile target with threat observation.
  - Observe / verify: Separate threat on shield application, actual absorption and unused expiry; do not attribute incidental healing or damage threat to the shield.
- **Medium · [WAR-009 — Sunder Armor AP threat coefficient](#war-009)**
  - Prerequisites: Same Sunder rank, stance/talents and enemy; two known AP values and precise threat API readings.
  - Observe / verify: Compare threat slopes over multiple applications, separating first application and refresh. No damage-based proxy is needed.
- **Medium · [WL-006 — Improved Imp's extra dummy effect](#wl-006)**
  - Prerequisites: A live Imp, ranks 0/1/2/3 of Improved Imp, fixed owner/pet haste and mana.
  - Observe / verify: Record Firebolt cast start/end and the interval before the next cast. Distinguish a shorter cast from removal of the engine's artificial 200-ms recast delay.
- **Low · [ROG-003 — Poison charge depletion](#rog-003)**
  - Prerequisites: A low-rank finite coating and combat/charge logging.
  - Observe / verify: Only if consumption semantics remain unclear: distinguish eligible weapon swings, proc attempts and landed poison hits, including resisted applications.

### Level-30 beta

An experiment requiring abilities or items by level 30. The October 1 notes announce that cap; actual access and prerequisites still need checking.

- **High · [DATA-001 — Server downranking penalties](#data-001)**
  - Prerequisites: The same spell/rank and controls at level 30.
  - Observe / verify: Check whether its SP slope changes as the player outlevels the rank. This extends the low-level test, not the level-60 conclusion.
- **High · [DRU-005 — Bear threat multipliers](#dru-005)**
  - Prerequisites: Primal Bite talent, available from 25.
  - Observe / verify: Isolate direct Bite damage and threat with the previously measured form multiplier.
- **High · [MAG-002 — Fingers of Frost in-flight timing](#mag-002)**
  - Prerequisites: Level 30, one point in Fingers, Frostbolt and precise cast/impact/aura timestamps.
  - Observe / verify: Compare waiting for impact with immediately starting the next cast, at short and long range. Count charge removal and Shatter outcomes for the already-started cast.
- **High · [WAR-001 — Level-60 outgoing rage normalization](#war-001)**
  - Prerequisites: A known weapon retained across levels and no other rage gains.
  - Observe / verify: Optional extrapolation checkpoint: compare uncapped rage per landed swing before and after leveling. This does not certify level 60.
- **High · [WAR-002 — Off-hand and extra-swing rage](#war-002)**
  - Prerequisites: A sourced extra-attack effect actually available by level 30, and separate MH/OH events.
  - Observe / verify: Isolate extra swings from regular autos and energizes. If no suitable effect is obtainable, defer that subtest rather than substituting ordinary swings.
- **High · [WL-001 — Demonic Brand power source and threat](#wl-001)**
  - Prerequisites: Level 25+ Brand, Imp and a melee demon, controlled owner school power and pet modifiers.
  - Observe / verify: Separate normal pet attacks from Brand events. Vary owner power, record Brand crits and threat, and test a second target without a Brand.
- **Medium · [DRU-008 — Nature's Grace GCD stacking and timing](#dru-008)**
  - Prerequisites: Nature's Grace, cooldown timestamps and controllable Wrath travel distance.
  - Observe / verify: Compare GCDs with the aura and an isolated cast-speed control; compare aura activation with cast completion and projectile impact.
- **Medium · [MAG-004 — Hot Streak interruption and new-charge ordering](#mag-004)**
  - Prerequisites: Level 25+ Hot Streak/Pyro build and cast/impact/aura logs.
  - Observe / verify: Start accelerated Pyro while an earlier Fire projectile is in flight; compare aura stacks at impact and completion. Separately cancel Pyro if interruption support is being evaluated.
- **Medium · [MAG-005 — Clearcasting and Missile Barrage event ordering](#mag-005)**
  - Prerequisites: Level 25+ Missile Barrage, controlled proc state.
  - Observe / verify: Compare channels with Clearcasting only, Barrage only and both, including a new proc during the channel. Record actual mana debit rather than tooltip cost.
- **Medium · [ROG-001 — Mutilate off-hand flat damage and Cold Blood](#rog-001)**
  - Prerequisites: Level 30 Mutilate/Cold Blood allocation, two known daggers, fixed AP and target armor.
  - Observe / verify: Record both child hit/crit outcomes with and without Cold Blood. Swap hand placements and vary AP independently to distinguish flat bonus from weapon contribution.
- **Medium · [ROG-002 — Rogue finisher and poison scaling](#rog-002)**
  - Prerequisites: Deadly Poison access and a controlled AP delta.
  - Observe / verify: Measure one-stack ticks and then five-stack ticks to locate the 0.0045 ratio. Audit finishers in separate AP/CP controls rather than mixing poison proc counts with their damage.
- **Medium · [ROG-005 — Hack and Slash hand scope and ICD](#rog-005)**
  - Prerequisites: One point in Hack and Slash at level 30; matched dagger/fist, mace and sword pairs.
  - Observe / verify: Swap MH/OH placement. Compare each hand's crit and armor-sensitive damage, plus a non-weapon spell control; separate a displayed character-sheet bonus from hand-specific outcomes.
- **Medium · [ROG-007 — Blade Flurry copied-damage modifiers](#rog-007)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-30 Blade Flurry, two controlled targets and a removable damage modifier.
  - Observe / verify: Compare primary and copied hits against equal and different armor. Toggle one attacker modifier and one target modifier separately; compare ratios rather than unrelated DPS totals.
- **Medium · [SHA-003 — Windfury Weapon extra-attack handling](#sha-003)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-30 Windfury Weapon, a known two-handed or one-handed MH weapon, no other extra-attack effect.
  - Observe / verify: Record the proc's two damage events, misses/crits/glances, regular swing timing and proc spacing. Change AP independently and keep the initial rank distinct from its max-scaled tooltip.
- **Medium · [SHA-006 — Flametongue Totem damage formula and comparison](#sha-006)**
  - Prerequisites: Rank-one Flametongue at level 28; several weapon speeds and known SP deltas.
  - Observe / verify: Measure on-hit fire damage and eligible white/special hits, removing other damage procs. Grace of Air is not available in this stage.
- **Medium · [WAR-010 — Weaponmaster hand-specific armor ignore](#war-010)**
  - Prerequisites: One-point Weaponmaster, comparable mace/non-mace weapons, matched AP and controlled target armor.
  - Observe / verify: Move the mace between hands and measure main-hand damage changes; separate the weapon's own damage change and sword extra attacks.

### Beyond level 30 / launch

Requires access beyond the announced level-30 beta or max-level content. Reclassify if later beta access is announced.

- **High · [CORE-001 — Boss attack tables](#core-001)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-60 characters and level-63 targets on a build without the known glancing defect.
  - Observe / verify: Repeat outcome and crit-suppression counts; compare damage of glances with ordinary hits at fixed AP.
- **High · [CORE-003 — Energy refunds on avoided attacks](#core-003)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-32+ Cat with Ferocious Bite.
  - Observe / verify: Separate initial cost, excess-Energy spending, refund and combo-point retention on avoided Bites.
- **High · [CORE-007 — Judgement of Wisdom trigger rules](#core-007)**
  - Prerequisites: A level-38+ Paladin with Seal/Judgement of Wisdom, uncapped mana recipients and isolated event sources.
  - Observe / verify: Count mana returns per white hit, avoided white, special, direct spell, periodic tick and triggered effect. Compare event intervals to distinguish chance from ICD; the level-30 cap does not grant this seal.
- **High · [CORE-011 — Base attributes and class conversions](#core-011)**
  - Prerequisites: Naked level-60 characters with racial/talent bonuses accounted for, plus isolated Agility/Intellect gear deltas.
  - Observe / verify: Record base attributes, health/mana and crit slopes for each class; race pairs isolate racial offsets.
- **High · [DATA-001 — Server downranking penalties](#data-001)**
  - Prerequisites: Level 60 and the actual downranked spells used by the retained APLs.
  - Observe / verify: Repeat the two-SP slope comparison for low and maximum ranks; separate learned-level base growth from the coefficient.
- **High · [DRU-003 — Form weapon damage and flat imbues](#dru-003)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-60 forms and high-level weapon effects if low-level results imply scaling.
  - Observe / verify: Verify the actual level-60 base and any effect-specific exceptions before changing synthetic-weapon valuation.
- **High · [DRU-005 — Bear threat multipliers](#dru-005)**
  - Prerequisites: Lacerate from 42 and eventually level-60 ranks.
  - Observe / verify: Separate application and bleed threat at each stack; distinguish flat threat from damage multipliers.
- **High · [DRU-006 — Lacerate direct and periodic formula](#dru-006)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-42+ Bear, stable AP, no other bleeds, isolated first through fifth applications.
  - Observe / verify: Determine whether the first application deals direct damage and whether subsequent hits use the pre-existing or new stack count; separately measure tick damage and crits.
- **High · [DRU-011 — Proc enchants in animal forms](#dru-011)**
  - Prerequisites: Crusader access if unavailable in either beta cap.
  - Observe / verify: Repeat the form comparison with enough eligible attacks to distinguish no procs from a low rate. Move earlier if vendors or copied items make the enchant obtainable.
- **High · [DRU-012 — Bear outgoing and incoming rage formulas](#dru-012)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-60 Bear and known outgoing/incoming attacks.
  - Observe / verify: Check that the low-level formula still fits; test queued Maul separately because it replaces the ordinary white event.
- **High · [MAG-002 — Fingers of Frost in-flight timing](#mag-002)**
  - Prerequisites: Level 31 for the second charge, unless later beta access is announced.
  - Observe / verify: Repeat with two charges; do not assume the one-charge observation establishes simultaneous refresh behavior.
- **High · [PAL-002 — Seal Echo coexistence and consumption](#pal-002)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-40+ Twist of Light, both relevant seals and aura/event logging.
  - Observe / verify: Replace seals before the next auto, record simultaneous Echo auras, then compare landed and avoided autos plus a Judgement-only control.
- **High · [PAL-003 — Windfury Totem proc and charge rules](#pal-003)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-32+ Shaman providing Totem, Paladin recipient, no weapon imbue or other extra-attack source.
  - Observe / verify: Count eligible autos, specials and seal events; record AP aura charges and the next normal swing. Isolate avoided events and exclude immediate recursion before estimating chance.
- **High · [PRI-001 — Shadow Word: Death script value 150](#pri-001)**
  - Prerequisites: Death rank one at level 32; fixed SP, talents and target mitigation.
  - Observe / verify: Compare damage and backlash above/below execute thresholds, lethal/nonlethal hits and cooldown behavior. Subtract ordinary Early Demise and damage-range effects before attributing anything to 150.
- **High · [SHA-001 — Maelstrom Weapon proc rate](#sha-001)**
  - Prerequisites: Level 35+ Enhancement; known rank, weapon speed and extra-attack sources.
  - Observe / verify: Count eligible landed swings/specials and added stacks; compare weapon speeds and talent ranks, recording Windfury separately. Move earlier only if beta access expands beyond 30.
- **High · [WAR-001 — Level-60 outgoing rage normalization](#war-001)**
  - Prerequisites: Level 60 and known one- and two-handed base speeds.
  - Observe / verify: Measure uncapped ordinary swings while varying damage independently; test the existing 4.5 and 4.5/1.3 rates rather than fitting a damage formula anew.
- **High · [WAR-002 — Off-hand and extra-swing rage](#war-002)**
  - Prerequisites: Relevant talent ranks and the actual raid Windfury buff.
  - Observe / verify: Repeat the off-hand ratio with the rage talent and test proc-generated swings, independently of damage and crit.
- **High · [WAR-003 — Incoming rage and mitigation](#war-003)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-60 Warrior and known incoming attacks.
  - Observe / verify: Repeat the selected low-level model at max level before certifying tank resource scaling.
- **High · [WAR-004 — Berserker Rage's extra incoming rage](#war-004)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-32+ Warrior, several known incoming hit sizes, fixed armor/health and no outgoing attacks.
  - Observe / verify: Compare rage with and without Berserker Rage separately for melee and spells; distinguish a constant bonus from a multiplier.
- **High · [WAR-006 — Flurry amount and charge events](#war-006)**
  - Prerequisites: Warrior level 35+ for the first rank; level 39 for rank five. Later beta access could move this earlier.
  - Observe / verify: Record aura stack changes and swing times for crits, avoided swings, paired MH/OH swings, HS and multi-target Cleave. Verify refresh/consumption ordering without assuming a 500-ms gate.
- **High · [WAR-008 — Shield attacks and weapon procs](#war-008)**
  - Prerequisites: Level-40 Shield Slam and access to the exact proc source, including level-32+ Windfury Totem where relevant.
  - Observe / verify: Repeat isolated attacks, separating landed/avoided outcomes and weapon versus shield effects.
- **High · [WL-001 — Demonic Brand power source and threat](#wl-001)**

  - Observe / verify: Complete ranked deltas and scaling with player level.

## Evidence and implementation follow-up

The individual records identify source-ready corrections separately from assumptions. No item marked Implementation gap has been silently fixed by this research publication.

- **[DATA-006 — Legacy item and enchant proc assumptions](#data-006)**: Add Crusader's sourced self-heal and stop the Strength formula increasing below level 60; leave PPM and proc eligibility separately qualified.
- **[DATA-010 — Raw haste rating conversion](#data-010)**: Represent raw haste rating separately from flat percentages, using the sourced level-60 conversion of 10 rating per percent.
- **[DATA-011 — Item-picker shared-crit EP](#data-011)**: Project shared equipment crit/hit into picker valuation exactly once, preserving explicitly scoped exceptions.
- **[DATA-008 — Unimplemented vendor item effects](#data-008)**: Implement Defender's Grip's ordinary outside-city 8% Block for 15 seconds; do not invent the other items' script behavior.

## Updating an answer

Edit `docs/uncertainties.json`, retaining the ID and qualified legacy references. Update the reviewed answer, confidence, remaining scope and concrete tests; distinguish an answered source question from outstanding implementation. Regenerate with `python3 tools/forever_bench/uncertainties.py`.

Old T50, T51 and T52 labels were reused for different topics. The qualified aliases below preserve those references without conflating their answers. Private chat and identifying logs stay local.

## Inventory coverage

- Read the legacy in-game checks, dispositions, demo checklist, all eleven class/shared/consumable beta-pass reports, mechanics/history/MythicSim/weekly/latest-upstream reviews and tank report. Screened the other top-level source, gear, race, Tier, haste, spell-inventory and patch reports for unresolved claims.
- Reviewed 137 spell-manifest records selected for assumed, unreviewed or uncertainty-bearing notes. A manifest label is provenance, not proof of an active bug: stale labels such as Bloodthrill's borrowed ID and Quick Strikes being absent are superseded by current code.
- Screened 267 matching runtime comment lines. Unknown-enum names, implementation-language assumptions and unrelated Classic/legacy encounter TODOs are not gameplay questions. Real-item proc/guardian notes remain source-indexed conditional work under DATA-006 and DATA-007.
- Generated historical build tables are not independent sources. Their current caveats are represented by class entries; old result counts, paid-hit conventions and unreplayed research are not relabeled as current evidence.
- Private chat and combat-log identifiers remain local. Public source links and the committed review conclusions provide the shareable evidence trail. This is consolidation and current-code reconciliation, not a fresh in-game verification of every mechanic.

### CORE-001 — Boss attack tables

**Needs evidence · High priority · Moderate confidence**

**Disposition:** Partly answered

**Question:** What are level-60 miss, dodge, parry, crit-suppression and glancing rules against level-63 targets?

**Finding:** An October 3 public measurement has 300 misses/4259 attacks against+3 targets at 1% hit:7.04%,95% Wilson about 6.31–7.85%. It supports an 8% rather than 9% single-weapon/special cap. This supersedes treating all suppression behavior as Classic-confirmed; ranged/dual-wield/boss-level scopes are not established by this sample.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Forever uses the explicit attack-table changes in the engine, with remaining inherited formulas. Demo columns and research checklists do not establish every boss case.

**Impact:** All melee, ranged and tank comparisons; hit caps and crit value.

**Remaining scope:** Direct raw-event outcome/skill controls, attack-type scope, level 60 suppression and separate dodge/parry/crit/glancing rules.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Treat suppression removal as a focused evidence-backed candidate, not a wholesale table replacement. Do not tune known glancing bugs or silently assume ranged/dual-wield equivalence.

**Current beta · level 30**
- Prerequisites: Known skill/hit, an equal-level and a +3-level target, recorded facing.
- Observe / verify: Count white/special/ranged outcomes separately; compare queued and unqueued attacks. This supplies a low-level table, not a level-63 certification.

**Beyond level 30 / launch**
- Prerequisites: Level-60 characters and level-63 targets on a build without the known glancing defect.
- Observe / verify: Repeat outcome and crit-suppression counts; compare damage of glances with ordinary hits at fixed AP.

### CORE-002 — Energy regeneration and haste

**Needs evidence · High priority · Low confidence**

**Disposition:** Game test needed

**Question:** Does general haste increase Energy regeneration, and do attack-speed-only effects leave it unchanged?

**Finding:** PowerType establishes the base 10 Energy/sec, not the haste coefficient. The previously analyzed 1% sample spans both 10 and 10.1/sec within endpoint quantization error. No new controlled source in the reviewed issue collections settles the distinction.

**Current implementation / scenario:** 10 Energy/sec integrated in 100-ms steps; general haste provisionally increases the rate. Slice and Dice, Berserking and attack-only enchants do not. The step size is not a measured server tick.

**Impact:** Feral and all Rogue builds; haste and resource value.

**Remaining scope:** General-haste scaling, distinct from attack-speed effects.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Keep the existing haste multiplier explicitly provisional; do not import retail resource rules as a fact.

**Current beta · level 30**
- Prerequisites: Two known general-haste totals, identical resource talents, uncapped recovery windows and precise resource timestamps.
- Observe / verify: Repeat matched recovery cycles from low Energy to below the cap, with no attacks or refunds. Aggregate endpoint uncertainty; a single rounded 1% window is insufficient. Run an attack-speed-only control separately.

### CORE-003 — Energy refunds on avoided attacks

**Needs evidence · High priority · Moderate confidence**

**Disposition:** Partly answered

**Question:** Which builders and finishers refund Energy on miss, dodge or parry, and what fraction of the paid cost returns?

**Finding:** The captured client distinguishes builders from finishers: Sinister Strike, Claw and Rake have the discount-on-miss attribute bit that Eviscerate, Rupture, Rip and Ferocious Bite lack. This supports the existing distinction, not a universal refund. It does not supply the server's refund percentage. Ferocious Bite first becomes available at 32, not in either announced beta cap.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Inherited 80% builder refunds; damaging finishers generally do not refund. Costs are charged before the outcome.

**Impact:** Feral and Rogue resource supply, especially before hit cap or when attacking from the front.

**Remaining scope:** The paid-cost refund fraction and combo-point retention for each affected family.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Retain the builder/finisher distinction. Compare actual paid cost after talents or Clearcasting, not nominal tooltip cost.

**Current beta · level 30**
- Prerequisites: A Rogue with builders/Eviscerate/Rupture, or a level-20 Cat with Claw/Rake/Rip; uncapped Energy and an avoidance-producing target.
- Observe / verify: Pair resource changes and combo points with each avoided action; subtract independently measured regeneration. Test builders and finishers separately.

**Beyond level 30 / launch**
- Prerequisites: Level-32+ Cat with Ferocious Bite.
- Observe / verify: Separate initial cost, excess-Energy spending, refund and combo-point retention on avoided Bites.

### CORE-004 — Spell GCD versus physical GCD

**Model assumption · High priority · Moderate confidence**

**Disposition:** Credible working answer

**Question:** Which speed effects shorten magical and physical GCDs, and what is the minimum?

**Finding:** The consistently applied physical-school versus magical-school rule is a reasonable accepted working model, corroborated by the pinned WoWSims parser. The client gives category 133 and 1500 ms for both shocks and Mortal Strike, so those fields cannot independently prove which GCDs scale. This is not a remaining per-spell implementation hunt.

**Current implementation / scenario:** The adopted WoWSims-style rule hastes magical GCDs with casting speed, retains fixed physical GCDs, and uses a one-second floor. Missing magical schools were corrected across the audited utility spells.

**Impact:** All rotations; especially instant Shaman spells and physical 1.5-second abilities.

**Remaining scope:** An optional empirical check of the shared rule and one-second floor; not separate tests for every spell with the same classification.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Keep the adopted rule and its regression coverage. Preserve the distinction between damage school and melee/ranged hit table.

**Current beta · level 30**
- Prerequisites: Known casting-speed modifier, one magical instant and one physical 1.5-second action; client cooldown timestamps.
- Observe / verify: Compare GCD duration independently of cast time. Only test the floor when enough haste is actually available; a 1% modifier cannot establish it.

**References:** [docs/speed_audit.md](https://github.com/gunba/wow-forever-sim/blob/forever/docs/speed_audit.md) · [docs/weekly_review.md](https://github.com/gunba/wow-forever-sim/blob/forever/docs/weekly_review.md) · [sim/core/cast.go](https://github.com/gunba/wow-forever-sim/blob/forever/sim/core/cast.go) · [sim/core/spell.go](https://github.com/gunba/wow-forever-sim/blob/forever/sim/core/spell.go)

**Earlier references:** T17 / T40 (GCD)

### CORE-005 — Channel speed sources

**Needs evidence · High priority · Moderate confidence**

**Disposition:** Partly answered

**Question:** Which general-haste effects compress channels, distinct from casting-speed-only effects?

**Finding:** The Berserking/Arcane Missiles observation and separate client attack/cast-speed auras support the current casting-speed versus channel-speed distinction. Current selected equipment has no raw SpellHaste source; the unverified general-haste channel multiplier therefore is not an unexplained benefit currently supplied by gear. This does not establish that every effect called haste behaves identically.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Separate SpellHaste scales supported channels provisionally. Berserking speeds hardcasts but not Arcane Missiles; Missile Barrage has its own explicit tick period. No selected item supplies raw SpellHaste.

**Impact:** Mage, Priest and Warlock channels; hypothetical haste scaling.

**Remaining scope:** Channel behavior of a specifically identified general-haste source, and extrapolation beyond the observed Berserking case.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Do not merge casting speed into SpellHaste. Keep future raw-rating support under DATA-010.

**Current beta · level 30**
- Prerequisites: Arcane Missiles and separately isolated Berserking or Wind Blessed; all missile timestamps.
- Observe / verify: Compare complete channel duration and tick spacing with a no-modifier control, excluding Missile Barrage.

**Sources / code**
- Prerequisites: A concrete obtainable general-haste effect or rating-bearing item.
- Observe / verify: Identify its aura types before scheduling a gameplay test. Acquisition is not established merely by the hypothetical SpellHaste stat; move to launch only if the chosen source requires it.

### CORE-007 — Judgement of Wisdom trigger rules

**Needs evidence · High priority · Low confidence**

**Disposition:** Game test needed

**Question:** Which events trigger Wisdom, at what probability and with what cooldown?

**Finding:** The mana amount is sourced: effect 698050 returns 59 at the highest rank. The proc probability is not settled by Wowhead's displayed 50%: all three captured SpellAuraOptions versions instead have 100% on the parent, which triggers dummy intermediate spell 1826. A server filter can exist behind that intermediate. Neither field proves the complete proc rule.

**Current implementation / scenario:** The level-60 return is 59 mana. The inherited event/proc model, including its 50% chance, remains provisional; self-hits are excluded.

**Impact:** Mana sustainability of melee Hunters, Paladins and other frequent attackers.

**Remaining scope:** Effective proc chance, avoided-white eligibility, periodic/proc eligibility and ICD.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Keep 50% explicitly provisional; do not replace it with 100% merely from the parent. The current code even allows avoided white swings, which needs its own event-category check.

**Beyond level 30 / launch**
- Prerequisites: A level-38+ Paladin with Seal/Judgement of Wisdom, uncapped mana recipients and isolated event sources.
- Observe / verify: Count mana returns per white hit, avoided white, special, direct spell, periodic tick and triggered effect. Compare event intervals to distinguish chance from ICD; the level-30 cap does not grant this seal.

### CORE-014 — Mana restoration threat

**Needs evidence · High priority · Moderate confidence**

**Disposition:** Partly answered

**Question:** Which mana returns generate threat, who receives it, and is it divided between enemies?

**Finding:** All registered Life Tap and Dark Sacrifice ranks carry client Attributes_1 NO_THREAT. A zero spell-damage threat multiplier did not prevent the separate mana-gain accumulator adding threat. Actual simulations reproduced phantom owner, pet and Priest threat; scoped accounting fixes pass without changing resource amounts. Charge is not registered locally, so no Charge implementation is claimed.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Explicit NoThreat resource metrics exclude Forever Life Tap (owner and demon transfers) and Dark Sacrifice from end-of-iteration mana threat. Other existing mana/rage allocation behavior is retained.

**Impact:** Tank TPS and rotation comparisons: wasting mana can increase subsequent effective restoration and its credited threat without improving damage or survival.

**Remaining scope:** Threat ownership, target distribution and source flags for other restoration effects; current Charge/mobility coverage is separate.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Keep explicit per-source flags rather than infer resource threat from damage multipliers. Ordinary gain accounting is unchanged; these fixes affect threat metrics, not mana supply or damage.

**Current beta · level 30**
- Prerequisites: A mana user, effective mana potions, threat API readings and one versus several engaged enemies.
- Observe / verify: Measure total and per-enemy threat from one isolated return, including same-type and mixed-type packs. A mana-capped use is the wasted-resource control.

### CORE-016 — Common player Spirit regeneration

**Accepted working answer · High priority · Moderate confidence**

**Disposition:** Credible working answer

**Question:** Do all player classes share the Mage/Priest formula, including its intercept?

**Finding:** Both Hunter pairs and five of six Paladin pairs fit 6.25 + Spirit/8, apart from roughly 0.001 in API output. The first Paladin pair would fit at 48 rather than its reported 49 Spirit; this single outlier does not establish a different Paladin intercept. The API dump omitted effective-Spirit and casting-regeneration values. A common-player formula is a better-supported provisional model, not proof for all classes or level 60.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Forever players use the common working formula 6.25 + effective Spirit/8 MPS. Explicit class overrides, pets, Classic regeneration and the separate MP5 contribution remain unchanged.

**Impact:** Mana pacing, talents and gear for non-Mage/Priest mana users.

**Remaining scope:** Effective versus first-return UnitStat values, fractional stats, levels, MP 5/buff controls and coverage of other classes/pets.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Implemented the provisional common-player formula without an API-offset fudge. Focused checks cover the consistent measurements, casting/noncasting Spirit, both MP5 modes, preserved explicit overrides and unchanged pet/Classic formulas. Refresh affected mana pacing and comparisons; retain the unmatched raw sample.

**Optional / conditional · Current beta · level 30**
- Prerequisites: Hunter/Paladin plus another mana class, several Spirit values, no MP5/buffs, sufficient mana deficit.
- Observe / verify: Capture all UnitStat returns, GetManaRegen values, build/level/race and timed actual regeneration both inside/outside five-second rule.

**Optional / conditional · Beyond level 30 / launch**
- Prerequisites: Unresolved higher-level classes/passives.
- Observe / verify: Repeat only remaining level/class terms rather than assume low-level intercept is universal.

**Finding:** The beta report supplies 0/2/4 gear-MP5 controls, a combat-log attachment and video; a project contributor acknowledges an engineering bug. It explicitly reports normal five-second behavior for Blessing of Wisdom and Mageblood. This is evidence for a gear-specific beta defect, not a universal redefinition of MP5.

**Impact:** Mana users if enabled; does not establish a current ranking error.

**Remaining scope:** Whether the gear bug has been deployed as fixed on a later build. That is a beta-version watch, not a prerequisite for the intended ordinary-MP5 benchmark.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** The default MP5/5 rule remains appropriate for the intended model. The optional uniform fivefold setting is a hypothetical sensitivity mode, not a faithful emulation of the reported gear-only bug; its description should say so.

**Optional / conditional · Current beta · level 30**
- Prerequisites: Only if reproducing a particular live beta build is needed; gear with a known MP5 delta and a separate Wisdom/Mageblood control.

### WAR-003 — Incoming rage and mitigation

**Needs evidence · High priority · Moderate confidence**

**Disposition:** Partly answered

**Question:** Does unmitigated damage × 10 / maximum health explain incoming rage at all armor/health values?

**Finding:** Public evidence confirms that receiving damage through one's own Priest shield still generates Warrior rage. It does not settle the amount: the incoming-rage issue contains both a damage/conversion-factor hypothesis and a pre-armor/max-health fit with an unexplained low-armor doubling. A developer response says incoming generation is under investigation. These are not interchangeable verified formulas.

**Current implementation / scenario:** That formula is used for Forever Warriors. The low-level doubled low-armor cluster and higher-level behavior remain unexplained; other classes retain their separate rules.

**Finding:** The no-external-buffs question is answered for both Hunter and Warlock pets by a direct report and an explicit Not A Bug response explaining the removal of pet buff upkeep. Focus base regeneration/cap are already client-backed. Pet AI scheduling is a separate simulation approximation, not missing evidence that pets need buffs.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Generic external player buffs are excluded under the adopted common pet model. Focus base regeneration/cap are client-backed; action scheduling is a simulator approximation.

**Impact:** Pet damage and resource waste; explicit pet talents remain valid exceptions.

**Remaining scope:** Ability scheduling/resource waste, and any explicitly targeted pet-only exceptions.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Close the generic external-buff question. Retain AI cadence as a named model approximation with optional sensitivity checks, not a mandatory repeat of buff eligibility tests.

**Current beta · level 30**
- Prerequisites: Only if pet cadence sensitivity proves material; a trained damage ability and a resource trace.
- Observe / verify: Compare ability use when resource-limited versus resource-capped. Do not mix this with owner inheritance or ordinary spell cooldowns.

### HUN-004 — Summon Hawk guardian model

**Accepted working answer · High priority · Moderate confidence**

**Disposition:** Credible working answer

**Question:** How do Hawk attacks, two-Hawk coexistence and inherited stats actually work?

**Finding:** Independent capture of all 222 encounters in public reports 2695/2701 supports two guardians, replacement, retargeting, minimum one-second opening travel and ranged-hasted assault timing. It finds 18 crits in 1,029 landed assaults, contradicting never-crit. These are October 2 observations, not proof of unchanged October 8 server behavior. The tested lifecycle implementation replaces the one-DoT surrogate; numerical rank-60 calibration remains provisional.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Two independent 18-second guardians with global oldest replacement, arrival attacks and owner ranged-speed inheritance. Opening uses always-hit, crit-capable damage after at least one second. Assault calibration is 0.35 × rank base, 2.5-second base swings and 1.5% effective crit; UF applies once, Ferocity assault transfer is unresolved.

**Impact:** Pet/Melee row and Hawk alternatives; major model-dependent build opportunity.

**Remaining scope:** Controlled RAP/talent/crit transfer, higher-rank scaling, boss glancing/crit behavior, exact retarget commands, racial/Tier effects and Lone Wolf coexistence. No current default combines Lone Wolf with Hawk.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Guardian lifecycle, travel, haste, attribution, reset and proc-isolation regressions pass. Quantify 0.30–0.40 damage and 1–3% effective-crit sensitivity; consider Ferocity assault transfer separately. Revalidate Hunter choices rather than treating the calibrated default as measured level-60 data.

**Optional / conditional · Level-30 beta**
- Prerequisites: Level 25+ Hunter with Summon Hawk; fixed target, RAP and pet settings.
- Observe / verify: Summon once, twice and a third time before expiry. Separate opening damage from each guardian's later events and record despawns. Repeat with different owner RAP/crit without changing the target.

**Optional / conditional · Beyond level 30 / launch**
- Prerequisites: Higher Hawk ranks and the actual role Tier effects.
- Observe / verify: Verify rank progression and Tier interactions after the low-rank guardian model is established.

### MAG-005 — Clearcasting and Missile Barrage event ordering

**Needs evidence · Medium priority · Moderate confidence**

**Disposition:** Partly answered

**Question:** How do channel ticks, last-charge consumption and simultaneous procs interact?

**Finding:** Missile Barrage and Blizzard initial-roll gaps were reproduced and fixed. Arcane Missiles children explicitly carry NOT_A_PROC (0x200), which conflicts with a blanket ban on their triggering Arcane Concentration; the cited zero-proc sample has only 32 missiles. Existing AM behavior is therefore retained, not silently removed.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Clearcasting retains its one-second ICD and cast-complete consumption. Missile Barrage now rolls on landed eligible hits, not cast completion. Blizzard has initial per-target AC-only hit rolls; periodic ticks do not create generic hit callbacks.

**Impact:** Arcane and hybrid resources; ordinary persistent-Clearcasting bug is already fixed.

**Remaining scope:** Arcane Missiles proc opportunities and free-channel/new-charge consumption ordering in live Forever. Client exceptions and the small community sample disagree.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Use the corrected landed-hit callback and isolated Blizzard parent rolls without manufacturing damage, hit counts, Winter’s Chill, FoF or item procs. Do not reject every passive or zero-cost AM child on an unsourced rule.

**Current beta · level 30**
- Prerequisites: Arcane Concentration, Arcane Missiles and mana/aura/tick logging without other proc talents.
- Observe / verify: Cast isolated complete and cancelled channels; count Clearcasting procs and identify whether a pre-existing proc is spent at channel start or completion.

**Level-30 beta**

### MAG-007 — Master of Elements base-cost refunds and batching

**Resolved · Medium priority · High confidence**

**Disposition:** Source-backed answer

**Question:** Do free casts refund mana, and can one simultaneous AoE batch refund repeatedly?

**Finding:** Primary SpellAuraOptions 29074 specifies ProcCategoryRecovery 9ms, versus Arcane Concentration’s 1000ms. The base-cost refund and batch limit were reproduced: free casts returned zero and three same-batch crits refunded three times. Focused corrections now match the sourced model.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Forever critical eligible hits refund the rank percentage of base mana cost, including free casts, with the sourced 9ms proc cooldown. Classic behavior is unchanged.

**Impact:** Mage mana pacing and AoE resource accounting.

**Remaining scope:** No remaining code/source discrepancy for these two rules; client alignment is not a fresh live-server measurement.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Base-cost refund includes free Forever casts; the first qualifying crit starts the 9ms cooldown. Resource amount, school/rank scope and Classic retention have focused regressions.

### ROG-006 — Premeditation expiry and Feint threat

**Outside current scenarios · Low priority · High confidence**

### WL-010 — Bane of Havoc damage copying

**Accepted working answer · High priority · Moderate confidence**

**Disposition:** Credible working answer

**Question:** Are copy scope, one-target limit and threat represented without duplicated modifiers?

**Finding:** Client driver supports outgoing owner direct/periodic damage and one marked target; the child is Shadow, cannot crit and ignores caster damage modifiers. These source-backed omissions are now implemented and regression-tested.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Copies 15% of actual qualifying owner damage as a separate Shadow event to the marked enemy, with a per-owner one-target limit. No recursive copies, pet/self/healing leakage or repeated damage modifiers.

**Impact:** Multi-target Warlock damage; no gain in the current one-target reference.

**Remaining scope:** Exact copied-damage mitigation/proc/threat behavior beyond explicit source fields.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Copy and ownership/lifecycle corrections pass focused direct/periodic two-target regressions. Ordinary copy threat and exact server copy-mitigation behavior remain qualified assumptions; the single-target reference is unaffected.

**Optional / conditional · Sources / code**
- Prerequisites: Two targets and two Warlocks with independent Havoc/Banes.
- Observe / verify: Check15%copy, expiry/replacement/caster ownership, direct and periodic damage, no duplicated mitigation/crit and no recursive proc chains.

**Optional / conditional · Current beta · level 30**
- Prerequisites: Havoc is available on the test character; otherwise defer access.
- Observe / verify: Measure copy and threat behavior with separate owner/pet/self-damage events and mitigation changes.

**Remaining scope:** Server SP/proc penalty curves versus spell and player level, including imported low-rank rotations.

### DATA-002 — Projected gear budget and stat prices

**Model assumption · High priority · High confidence**

**Disposition:** Scenario decision

**Question:** How representative is equal modeled item cost across physical, caster and tank stats?

**Finding:** The gear-generation proof reproduces the captured armor/weapon quantity tables, but the allocation exponent, stat prices, Stamina shares and passive-trinket budget are explicit modeling choices. Equal modeled cost is not evidence of equal real-world gearing opportunity or equal DPS. Current requests contain projected equipment, not hidden real-item procs or a paid-hit conversion.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Hypothetical level-65 items use sourced quantity/armor/weapon tables but assumed nonlinear allocation budgets and special-stat prices. Equal cost is not equal DPS, and Intellect is not generic SP.

**Impact:** All cross-class rankings and gear scaling; tank defensive coverage must not be fabricated.

**Remaining scope:** Representativeness of the chosen budget and templates, not an unknown combat mechanic.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Keep the spreadsheet, per-item allocation proofs and legal armor constraints visible. Assess alternative prices as separate scenarios; replace assumptions only when enough current item observations constrain them.

**Sources / code**
- Prerequisites: A proposed alternative budget or additional sourced crafted/PvP items.
- Observe / verify: Fit out-of-sample items and compare total selected stat budgets by role; do not judge equivalence from the final DPS ranking.

### DATA-006 — Legacy item and enchant proc assumptions

**Needs evidence · Medium priority · High confidence**

**Disposition:** Partly answered

**Question:** Which inherited handlers still use assumed PPM, triggers or obsolete effect values?

**Finding:** This is material even with synthetic weapons: current requests equip 120 Crusader enchant copies and 28 Fiery copies. Crusader's client spell explicitly contains a 75–125 self-heal alongside 100 Strength for 15 seconds, but the handler implements only Strength. Its unbounded below-60 formula also grants more than 100 Strength at lower levels. Fiery's 40 base damage is sourced; its 6 PPM and Crusader's 1 PPM are not established by those effect amounts.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Numerous real-item handlers retain explicit assumptions; some source-supported amount updates are known but not imported. Synthetic weapons/trinkets have no implicit item procs, but their selected enchants can supply proc effects.

**Impact:** Manual catalog items and proc enchants on the projected gear pool. Form-specific enchant eligibility is tracked separately.

**Remaining scope:** Effective proc frequency, special/extra-attack eligibility, form handling and healing resolution/threat. Legacy real-item amount updates remain a separate dormant catalog backlog.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Add the sourced Crusader heal and correct the below-60 Strength arithmetic with targeted regressions before a later affected tank refresh. Lifestealing's health-leech effect is also reduced to damage-only, but no current profile equips it. Do not interpret a proc wrapper's 100% field as a 100%-per-swing rate.

**Sources / code**
- Prerequisites: Crusader enchant 1900 → spell 20007; fixed proc events at levels 20 and 60.
- Observe / verify: Check 100 Strength, the sourced self-heal range, health capping and damage/threat separation. Verify Lifestealing's heal separately if that enchant is enabled.

**Beyond level 30 / launch**
- Prerequisites: Actual Crusader/Fiery enchants, fixed-speed weapons and separate white-only, special-attack and extra-swing samples. Move earlier only if the beta supplies these high-skill enchants.
- Observe / verify: Estimate probability by eligible event type and weapon speed; record haste, handedness and form. A triggered spell's coefficient does not establish its PPM.

**Model assumption · Medium priority · High confidence**

**Disposition:** Scenario decision

**Question:** Do identical copies stack additively or multiplicatively?

**Finding:** Each Arcanum supplies 1% attack speed, not general Energy haste. The competing two-copy totals are 1.02 and 1.0201: only 0.009804% relative swing-speed difference. Exact stacking is not worth a standing high-effort gameplay test for this benchmark; that numerical bound is not a claim that every possible thresholded rotation has identical DPS.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Each grants attack speed only; identical copies add. Neither is general Energy haste.

**Impact:** Melee/ranged swing rates with two copies.

**Remaining scope:** The exact server stacking law remains unmeasured. Reopen if a stronger stacking effect or demonstrated material timing threshold depends on it.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Retain the additive convention as a negligible-range model choice, not a verified multiplicative-aura rule.

### DATA-011 — Item-picker shared-crit EP

**Implementation gap · Medium priority · High confidence**

**Disposition:** Known implementation work

**Question:** Does the gear picker value generic crit for casters the way the engine does?

**Finding:** The picker still directly dot-products the stored item stats against EP weights. The engine first shares equipment crit/hit between physical and spell fields. A caster with zero MeleeCrit weight therefore can undervalue an item whose generic crit is stored there. This is a reproducible valuation mismatch, not missing caster crit in combat.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Engine sharing works, but the picker can dot-product the unprojected MeleeCrit field against zero caster weight. This is a display/valuation limitation, not missing simulated crit.

**Impact:** Manual item sorting; native coordinate simulations are not driven by that displayed EP.

**Remaining scope:** Picker valuation/cache alignment with the actual equipment projection, including enchants and random suffixes.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Use the same shared-stat semantics once and retain scope-specific exceptions such as ranged scopes. Simulator-driven gear searches are not using this picker EP as their DPS result.

**Sources / code**
- Prerequisites: Generic-crit equipment with only a SpellCrit EP weight, plus ranged-only scope control.
- Observe / verify: Compare predicted picker deltas to the projected equipment stats. Check that sharing is neither omitted nor applied twice.

### SCEN-001 — Tank boss damage and external healing

**Model assumption · High priority · High confidence**

**Disposition:** Scenario decision

**Question:** What incoming damage and healing should define a representative tank comparison?

**Finding:** The incoming-damage and healing values are explicit controlled workloads, not claims about a known raid boss. The single workload is 300 seconds with one 3000-base/2-second attacker and 1500 external HPS; the multi workload is 90 seconds with three 1500-base/2-second attackers and 2500 HPS. There is no unique game-mechanics experiment that can prove these are the representative encounter.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Explicit stress scenarios: one 300-second boss or three 90-second attackers with fixed swing/AP/armor/healing settings. These are not observed raid bosses or healer behavior.

**Impact:** Tank DPS, rage, mana, threat and death rates; cannot be silently equated with un-attacked DPS rows.

**Remaining scope:** Which workloads are useful comparisons, and future measured encounter inputs.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Keep exact requests and per-target threat/survival outputs. Older tables in the original tank document describe superseded models; current request artifacts are authoritative.

**Sources / code**
- Prerequisites: A chosen workload or credible raid-log encounter specification.
- Observe / verify: Change damage/healing assumptions as a separately labeled scenario and compare matched inputs, rather than silently redefining the tank benchmark.

### SCEN-003 — Tank target selection and threat coverage

**Implementation gap · High priority · High confidence**

**Disposition:** Known implementation work

**Question:** Can a tank maintain threat on the weakest-covered enemy rather than repeatedly attacking the first?

**Finding:** This is an APL capability gap, not unknown game behavior. The available unit references do not provide a lowest-threat target selector. Saved multi-target tank results demonstrate why total TPS cannot substitute for the weakest add's threat.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Existing Warrior multi-target presets remain single-target focused; summed TPS masks very low threat on an add. No lowest-threat target selector is provided.

**Impact:** First-class AoE tank support and meaningful optimization.

**Remaining scope:** Explicit target selection/cycling with target-local debuffs and threat coverage.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Define a selector policy and use target-specific state; preserve self-maintained Sunder on the intended target. Do not infer raid aggro control solely from one player's total threat.

**Sources / code**
- Prerequisites: A three-target fixture with deliberately unequal per-target threat and debuff durations.
- Observe / verify: Check selection, switching, maintenance and minimum target TPS; ensure current-target lookups do not accidentally read the first target's aura.

### SCEN-002 — Non-tank external healing abstraction

**Model assumption · Medium priority · High confidence**

**Disposition:** Scenario decision

**Question:** How should health costs constrain Life Tap, Death and self-damaging consumables in DPS scenarios?

**Finding:** Non-tanking Life Tap deliberately does not debit health; tanking Life Tap pays the sourced health cost. Death and consumable self-hits are excluded from enemy DPS, while health depletion follows the core's configured survival model. The non-tank benchmark therefore assumes health support; it does not establish sustainable healer burden or survival.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Self-damage is excluded from enemy DPS. Non-tanking resource use retains its external-healing abstraction rather than a finite healer budget; tank requests pay real health costs.

**Impact:** Resource sustainability and practical healer burden.

**Remaining scope:** Whether to add a finite-healing DPS scenario, not whether self-damage should be counted as boss damage.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Expose the health-support abstraction and preserve self-damage accounting. A constrained healer budget would be a new scenario and could alter resource-limited rotations.

**Sources / code**
- Prerequisites: An explicit incoming-damage/healer-resource model and failure condition for non-tanks.
- Observe / verify: Compare paid health, effective healing, overheal and deaths separately from outgoing enemy damage.

### SCEN-010 — Forced Tier 1 and synthetic stat scaling

**Model assumption · Medium priority · High confidence**

**Disposition:** Scenario decision

**Question:** What do the Tier-off and +10%/+50% scenarios establish?

**Finding:** The three sensitivity scenarios already have a precise mathematical interpretation. Tier-off removes the role override, and +10%/+50% multiply item stats and weapon damage while keeping other inputs fixed. Amplification divides the equal-race-weight +50% gain by five times the +10% gain; it rejects negligible/noisy/nonpositive denominators. This measures finite-range curvature, not isolated synergy or exponential growth.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Full role Tier 1 is forced independently of equipment. Stat/weapon scaling holds enchants/procs/talents/APLs fixed; amplification is finite-range curvature, not proof of exponential growth or future loot.

**Impact:** Interpretation of all matrix gain columns.

**Remaining scope:** These controlled scenarios do not forecast future loot mixtures, cap changes, proc gear or reoptimized rotations.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Retain paired requests and hash-checked baseline association. A new gearing distribution is a new scenario, not a reinterpretation of the current column.

### SCEN-009 — Geometry, movement, kills and latency

**Outside current scenarios · Low priority · High confidence**

**Disposition:** Outside current scenarios

**Question:** Which real fight events are absent from the stationary benchmark?

**Finding:** Terrain, movement paths, add deaths and human latency are deliberately absent from the stationary reference workloads. Their exact real-world behavior cannot alter a run containing none of those events. This does not make Consecration damage or current three-target threat irrelevant.

**Current implementation / scenario:** No terrain/vertical targeting, realistic movement path, encounter add deaths or general player latency. AoE uses target/range approximations; remainingTime is encounter time, not per-target TTK.

**Impact:** Consecration placement, cone targeting, grenades, kill procs, stealth/control and short-lived adds.

**Remaining scope:** These become requirements for a moving/add-lifetime encounter, not current coefficient tests.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Keep the encounter scope visible and do not interpret encounter remainingTime as measured target TTK.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Owned Power Infusion can target a selected friendly unit. Omitted target defaults to self; explicitly unassigned disables it. The magic-damage/healing bonus and mana reduction do not stack with another PI provider. Native target and overlap checks pass.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Keep the maintenance fix; do not restore mana waste merely to reproduce old threat numbers.

### WAR-013 — Protection next-swing queue bypass

**Resolved · High priority · High confidence**

**Disposition:** Previously resolved

**Question:** Did the Protection APL add Heroic Strike/Cleave damage without replacing a white swing?

**Finding:** The selected Protection actions use the queue entries, and direct APL invocation of the damage components is rejected. This fixes the demonstrated extra-damage/rage bypass without asserting that every rage formula is correct.

**Current implementation / scenario:** Both actions use their queue entries in all ten Protection profiles. An on-next-swing flag rejects direct APL casts of Heroic Strike, Cleave and Maul damage components. Fury and Bear already used the correct queue entries.

**Impact:** The old Protection DPS, rage availability and threat were inflated. Earlier selection-gain claims are invalid; current results use corrected inputs.

**Remaining scope:** Historical validation uncertainty is covered by SCEN-016; it does not undo the reproduced queue bug or its structural fix.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Retain the corrected tags and queue guard. Do not reclassify normal queued attacks as a new rage exploit.

### WAR-014 — Protection Sunder maintenance starvation

**Resolved · High priority · High confidence**

**Disposition:** Previously resolved

**Question:** Does the Protection rotation preserve five Sunder stacks under competing rage demands?

**Finding:** The current APL reserves rage and gives Sunder an eight-second refresh window. The archived observer and reproduced-lapse regression support a substantial reduction in starvation, not an absolute guarantee against every avoidance/resource sequence.

**Current implementation / scenario:** An eight-second refresh window and dynamic-cost rage reserves substantially reduce lapses, with no free external armor debuff. Essential defenses retain priority.

**Impact:** In matched coverage samples, five-stack losses fall from 42.22% to 0.57% of single-attacker fights. Mean post-ramp time below five falls from 4.86 to 0.053 seconds.

**Remaining scope:** None for the reproduced priority defect. The residual rare lapse is disclosed rather than hidden with an external armor debuff.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Keep the resolved status and the measured, nonzero residual-lapse qualification. This review's resource-threat leads do not justify silently rerunning or relabeling its archived numbers.

**References:** [docs/protection_sunder.md](https://github.com/gunba/wow-forever-sim/blob/forever/docs/protection_sunder.md) · [tools/forever_bench/sunder_maintenance_test.go](https://github.com/gunba/wow-forever-sim/blob/forever/tools/forever_bench/sunder_maintenance_test.go) · [tools/sunder_audit/main.go](https://github.com/gunba/wow-forever-sim/blob/forever/tools/sunder_audit/main.go)

### DONE-010 — Seal of Command SP placement comparison

**Resolved · Medium priority · High confidence**

**Disposition:** Previously resolved

**Question:** Does this engine omit the 70% multiplier on personal SP that upstream added?

**Finding:** Seal of Command's personal SP contribution already passes through its 0.7 damage multiplier. The upstream placement change therefore does not establish an omitted multiplier here. Target Holy bonus is a separate later calculation.

**Current implementation / scenario:** No: proc DamageMultiplier is 0.7 × Improved Seals × weapon specialization, with BonusCoefficient 0.29. Personal SP passes through that multiplier; target Holy bonus is applied separately afterward.

**Impact:** A recent review overstated the difference by comparing field placement rather than final math. Righteousness remains genuinely unresolved.

**Remaining scope:** Independent seal trigger/scaling questions do not justify multiplying personal SP by 0.7 twice.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** No correction to this traced multiplier-placement claim.

### PAL-015 — Swift Judgement cooldown timing

**Resolved · Medium priority · High confidence**

**Disposition:** Previously resolved

**Question:** Does Protection actually exploit Swift Judgement’s reset and free cast?

**Finding:** The cooldown reset already functioned; explicit sequencing now spends the free Judgement promptly rather than resetting an almost-complete cooldown. The same-timestamp regression directly supports that implementation claim.

**Current implementation / scenario:** The reset already worked. Explicit APL placement now avoids resetting a nearly completed cooldown and casts the free Judgement before unrelated cooldowns.

**Impact:** About 31.5 to 35 Judgements per five minutes; roughly 5–6 DPS from the APL alone with shared support.

**Remaining scope:** Historical pooled uncertainty must respect overlapping seed ranges; no new timing-source gap was identified.

**Implementation / model follow-up:** Keep the sequencing fix and the SCEN-016 qualification on old comparison statistics.
